slides.title: MASS: Deep Research for Social Sciences with Memory-Augmented Social Simulation
slides.tldr: MEMORY-AUGMENTED SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR SOCIAL SCIENCE RESEARCH
slides.highlight: This work introduces MASS, a paradigm using realistic social simulations and memory mechanisms to enhance the creativity and empirical foundation of LLM-generated research, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: MASS enhances social science research agents by generating original empirical data through memory-augmented social simulations.
card.key_idea: Integrates dynamic goal-path planning, a 300K-entry multi-disciplinary behavior dataset for agent cold-start, and an Ebbinghaus-inspired structured forgetting mechanism to ensure authentic social simulations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DeepResearch Bench; showed 6.81% higher overall quality than foundation LLMs and 17.19% higher insight than strong baselines.
card.limitation: High computational cost and runtime for large-scale simulations, alongside risks of hallucinations in text generation and agent decision-making.

slides.title: Hierarchical Policies from Verbal and Egocentric Human Signals for Natural Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: The EDITH framework integrates first-person view, gaze, and speech to improve human-robot interaction, reducing user effort by utilizing nonverbal signals. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: EDITH enables robots to interpret human intent by combining verbal instructions with egocentric view and gaze signals.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical policy using a VLM high-level controller to generate subtasks (fine-grained instructions + grounding keyframes) and a VLA low-level controller for execution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three HRI tasks; achieved 59.7% average success rate, significantly outperforming language-only baselines (<6.5%) and reducing user workload (p < 0.001).
card.limitation: Reactivity is limited by VLM window-processing latency and performance degrades for users with physical attributes (e.g., height) different from training data.

slides.title: UBTECH launches UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions
slides.tldr: UBTECH RELEASES UWORLD U1 HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: The launch of UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions provides a reference for embodied social robots relevant to RwB.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA UNCERTAINTY-GUIDED LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework enhances proactive robot assistance in household environments by combining Markov models with LLM reasoning to handle noisy conditions. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight framework combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered when model confidence falls below a predefined threshold.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and the new HOMER-Noise dataset against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using F1-scores; results show competitive accuracy and superior noise robustness.
card.limitation: Inference latency is significantly higher than baselines due to external LLM API calls.

slides.title: Vietnam's Vingroup Unveils Two Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: Vingroup has introduced a guide bot and a factory bot, providing examples of humanoid applications relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: IRAF: Interference-Resilient Adaptive Fusion for Noise-Robust End-to-End Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This work introduces IRAF, a module that improves full-duplex interaction by modulating user audio contributions to handle interfering speakers. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: IRAF improves end-to-end full-duplex dialogue systems by gating user audio to resist interfering-speaker noise.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module predicts a frame-level reliability gate using target-speaker and user audio embeddings to rescale user representations before fusion with agent text embeddings.
card.evaluation: Tested on MS-MARCO and InstructS2S-200K using BLEU, sBERT, and turn-taking metrics; IRAF outperformed clean and noise-augmented baselines across various SNR levels.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and human-centered considerations into robot behavior to improve social acceptability. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for generating socially-aware robot motions that balance physical safety, fluency, and human acceptability.
card.key_idea: An MPC-based controller using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-based human motion prediction, parameterized by maximum velocity and interaction distance to create four distinct social behaviors.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-expert participants using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.
card.limitation: Interaction distance had minimal effect on most perceptual dimensions compared to the significant impact of velocity profiles.

slides.title: Decoupling Thought from Speech: Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Resilient Multi-Agent Argumentation
slides.tldr: ENHANCING MULTI-AGENT ARGUMENTATION RESILIENCE VIA ARCHITECTURAL DECOUPLING
slides.highlight: This work introduces Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning to prevent logic degradation and role drift in multi-agent debates, supporting MIMIC's focus on stable LLM-based agent models in societal-scale simulations.

card.one_liner: KG-CFR improves multi-agent debate resilience by decoupling private planning from public execution using knowledge grounding.
card.key_idea: A dual-stage architecture separating a private, retrieval-augmented counterfactual planning buffer from a public execution layer, utilizing recency bias to inject strategies at the context window's end.
card.evaluation: Tested in DRAU (1v1v1 environment) across 270 trajectories. Used LLM judges and custom metrics; quality rose from 0.694 to 0.822 with >95% shock resilience.
card.limitation: Increased inference latency, high token overhead, limited to tripartite topologies, and ineffective against affective (ad-hominem) perturbations.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR SAFE PHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that ensures trajectory accuracy and joint-limit safety during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines feedforward nonlinear inversion to create a constant-state linear plant with a Kalman-augmented MPC for predictive disturbance rejection and constraint handling.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a 7-DOF Franka FR3; showed <0.05mm steady-state error vs 44.8mm for classical impedance under 15N force; robust to 30% inertial mismatch.
card.limitation: Validated only in simulation; formal anti-windup proofs under persistent saturation and physical hardware validation are left for future work.
